target_claim: Running (revisit-permitting) Dijkstra on the explicitly constructed Gn performs 2^(n-2)-1 distinct relaxation updates to the sink vn's distance, hence Omega(2^n) Relax operations on this family.
source_quote:
There
are 2 n−2 −1 nonempty subsets of {v2, . . . , vn−1}, so the edge relaxations vi →vn (for
i = 2, 3, . . . , n −1) account for 2 n−2 −1 updates to vn’s distance alone.
test_sketch: Implement the exact construction (vertices v1..vn; w(v1->vn)=W, w(v1->vi)=0, w(vi->vn)=W-delta_i, w(vi->vj)=-delta_i for i<j, delta_i=2^(i-2), W=sum delta_i) and the described modified Dijkstra that re-inserts a vertex whenever its tentative distance improves. Instrument counters for (a) total Relax invocations and (b) successful updates to d(vn). For n=6,8,10,12 the trace settles v2..v_{n-1} once each in increasing key order, so d(vn) is updated only n-2 times and total relaxations are Theta(n^2) (each edge relaxed once, matching the solution's own admission 'the overall relaxation count is Θ(n2)'), versus the claimed 2^(n-2)-1 sink updates (e.g. n=12: observed 10 sink updates vs claimed 1023; total relax ~66 vs Omega(2^12)). Operation counts across n show polynomial, not exponential, growth, refuting the stated bound.
